title: MinuteProof hackathon demo (3 minutes, novice viewer)

decisions.decision: Heart (Kokoro af_heart, stock voice profile heart) at --speed 1.0; room tone, reverb and microphone character explicitly on at their subtle defaults.
decisions.note: Relayed by the team lead. Pace does not apply to Kokoro.

decisions.decision: Target 180 s, ceiling 200 s (ceiling an assumption).
Captions off, chapter titles off, no music.
Narrated image cards with the exact script text, rendered from demo/cards/cards.html in the product theme; title cards cannot hold 306 characters or line breaks.
decisions.note: Outro tail 3000 ms, the runtime maximum (script asked about 3.5 s).

decisions.decision: Scene 5 split into open-card, first-flag and source-page chapters with the same words, so each result is heard after its check.

The real click opens the PDF in a new tab; the scenario closes that tab and shows the same address in the recorded tab (only the scenario tab is recorded). Installed Chrome (--browser chrome) renders the PDF.
Capture with prefers-reduced-motion so the page stops its looping pulse and arrow; counters show final values and the card click jumps.
1600 x 900 (16:9) instead of the assumed 1440 x 900.
Pointer, press rings and idle fade only in scene 5 clicks (open-card, and source-page before the page changes); smoothing is authored.
decisions.note: Within the user decision: scene 5 clicks only.

decisions.decision: One review round (rounds.max 1): the user is almost out of time.
Local delivery copy at /Users/ethan/Downloads/minuteproof-demo-2026-11-04-v1.mp4; nothing uploaded.
maxQuietShare 0.35 (default 0.3): the quiet stretches are deliberate reading holds for a novice audience.
decisions.note: Chosen by the user on 2026-11-04, relayed by the team lead. v1 stays the delivery; no new take.

scenes.narration: At the top: seven hundred eighteen pages of minutes became one hundred twenty-eight red flags. A red flag is something a buyer or funder should worry about.

scenes.outcome: The wharf is the problem that kept coming back, and it is still put off.
scenes.narration: Next: what keeps coming back. The top issue is the Nielsen Park wharf and its pool piles, the posts in the water. It was raised at fourteen meetings, from nineteen seventy-two to nineteen seventy-five, and flagged nineteen times. Each dot is a meeting. Red dots were flagged. The latest, in March nineteen seventy-five, is a dangerous old pile stump. It's still deferred, meaning put off.
scenes.wait: About 1 s of smooth scrolling before the voice.
scenes.transition: Stays; the next chapter clicks the card.
scenes.focus: region and text: spotlight on the wharf card, then boxes on the headline (meetings, years, flags), the timeline dots and the latest entry as each is named

scenes.outcome: How it works in four plain steps, and the takeaway.
scenes.narration: Here's how it works. One: Reducto reads every page. Two: it pulls out each decision, repair, dollar amount and dispute, and notes its page. Three: DuckDB groups them over time, to find what keeps coming back. Four: every claim links to its page. Here, the reading took about six minutes. Hundreds of pages of board minutes became a cited red-flag report in minutes.
scenes.wait: About 1 s of scrolling before the voice.
scenes.focus: region: each of the four steps boxed as One, Two, Three, Four are said, then the extraction time
